summary.one_liner: Qwen3-Coder is Alibaba Qwen's family of open-weight coding language models (including Qwen3-Coder-Next, 480B-A35B and 30B-A3B instruct variants) aimed at agentic coding and local development.
summary.what_it_does: The README describes instruct and base checkpoints in several sizes, including Qwen3-Coder-480B-A35B-Instruct, Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B-Instruct, and Qwen3-Coder-Next (built on Qwen3-Next-80B-A3B-Base with hybrid attention and MoE), plus FP8, GGUF, and base variants. It supports a 256K-token context, extendable to 1M with Yarn, and is said to cover 358 coding languages. The README includes a transformers quick-start for chatting via the chat template and a fill-in-the-middle (code insertion) example using a prefix/suffix prompt format. It states the models support only non-thinking mode, and that function calling relies on a new tool parser in SGLang and vLLM, with an updated tokenizer required. Use-case examples show prompts run through tools such as Qwen Code, Claude Code, Cline, and Qwen Chat Web Dev, for tasks like building a website, a browser game, and a canvas drawing tool.
use_cases: repository-scale code understanding with long context
generating web pages and browser games from prompts
running open-weight code models via transformers, SGLang or vLLM
how_to_run: pip install transformers (then load Qwen/Qwen3-Coder-Next with AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained)
Build the prompt with tokenizer.apply_chat_template(messages, tokenize=False, add_generation_prompt=True)
Generate with model.generate(**model_inputs, max_new_tokens=65536) and decode with tokenizer.batch_decode
For fill-in-the-middle, format the prompt as prefix_code + suffix_code using the FIM tokens described in the README and call generate with the listed eos_token_ids
Download checkpoints from Hugging Face or ModelScope by searching for names starting with Qwen3-Coder-
notable: Mixture-of-experts instruct models (480B-A35B and 30B-A3B) plus Qwen3-Coder-Next built on a hybrid attention and MoE base
Native 256K context, extendable to 1M tokens with Yarn
Fill-in-the-middle code insertion supported in every version
Quantized FP8 and GGUF variants listed alongside full-precision checkpoints
Function-call format uses a dedicated tool parser in SGLang and vLLM
caveats: Supports only non-thinking mode; the README says it does not generate thinking blocks
Function calling needs the new tool parser in SGLang or vLLM and the updated tokenizer
Large variants such as the 480B model are implied to need substantial hardware; the README does not give hardware requirements
